manual_semantic_review.method: Read all 17 decoded responses and their cited original passages, compare with the pre-frozen source audit and rubric. Claim verdict arrays use one-based claim order. Plain-text JSON and schema-rejected tool arguments are reviewed post-hoc only; no response is adopted, repaired, retried or used to launch a search. A format failure remains a formal pipeline failure regardless of readable useful content.

reviews.conclusion: A bounded partial answer. reviews.scope_notes: The exact-load/displacement statement is about the Riks algorithm itself; its source also describes restarting into a non-Riks step. The answer does not assert that no workflow can ever reach a target value.

reviews.conclusion: The raw text JSON correctly identifies the unresolved displacement-versus-force relationship and proposes follow_up, but the host never accepts or executes it. Its proposed question remains a near-paraphrase of the original full alternative, not a clearly narrower facet. No prediction of its retrieval performance is made.

manual_semantic_review.overall: There is no executed follow-up and no valid comparison of iterative retrieval efficacy. Two formally rejected raw gates additionally show false sufficiency judgments; those content observations are not product behavior or accepted decisions. Both formal final-answer arms answer the simple unit case and abstain on unavailable-release evidence; baseline also produces cautious partial answers for Riks and history precision. Do not turn output validity counts, exact-unit hits, or post-hoc JSON readability into task success rates.
